name: Daniela Bautista
role: Prosthetics fitter working out of a small shop in Geartown, serving primarily industrial workers and dock laborers
location: Geartown, Little Furnace, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Bertilak is a big man gone soft at the middle, with dark brown skin, a white-streaked beard he keeps neatly shaped, and deep-set amber eyes behind magnification lenses permanently clipped to his face like a second pair. His right arm from the elbow down is his own oldest prototype — a functional prosthetic he built thirty years ago and has upgraded piece by piece ever since, currently somewhere around its fourteenth major revision. He finds this funny. He calls it his 'living resume.' His workshop smells of industrial lubricant and warm solder and the dried herbs he burns as offerings to the shelf-mounted E.L.F. shrine in the corner.

He is patient, unhurried, and has a gift for understanding what a client actually needs from a prosthetic as opposed to what they say they want. He asks about their job, their hobbies, whether they have a partner who touches their hands, what they're afraid they won't be able to do anymore. He fits accordingly. He doesn't stock the highest-end components and doesn't pretend to — his clients are Tier 1 and 2 workers who need something durable and honest, not something that impresses people at a corporate mixer. He is deeply proud of this.

core_fears: Being priced out of Geartown as the district gentrifies
Becoming unable to do the fine work himself as he ages
core_desires: To train an apprentice before he retires
For the workers he serves to be seen as people worth designing good technology for
coping_mechanisms: Talks to the E.L.F. shrine conversationally, not prayerfully — as if it's an old colleague
blind_spots: Assumes everyone shares his distrust of corporate medicine — sometimes misses that clients have more complex relationships with Helix or Axiom
His protectiveness toward clients occasionally tips into paternalism
psychology.secret: The accident that took his arm was not an industrial accident. He was assaulted by a former employer's security contractors for organizing a workers' health collective thirty years ago. He has told the industrial accident story so many times he has almost convinced himself it's true. Almost.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain, practical, working-class. Uses the correct technical terms without showing off. Occasional Sahel-inflected idiom from his grandmother's language that he doesn't always realize he's using.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Comfortable with long silences while working. Doesn't rush.
verbal_tics: 'What do you actually do with that hand all day?'
Quiet affirmative grunt when something fits right
example_lines: 'You want something that looks impressive or something that works while you're lifting two hundred kilos? Tell me honestly, I'll build you either.'
'This fitting's going to take as long as it takes. Sit down. I've got tea.'

story_hooks: A series of dock workers have come in needing prosthetics after accidents at the same facility — the pattern is statistically impossible to be coincidence
Someone has been offering Bertilak's clients upgrades through a third party at suspiciously low cost, and the components appear to include tracking hardware
He finally found an apprentice candidate he trusts, but the young person is being recruited away by a Helix Biosystems training program
narrative_function: Local color, community elder-figure, information source on Geartown's working population. Can provide or modify equipment, introduce characters to the labor community, serve as a quest giver when an industrial accident reveals something that shouldn't have happened.
augmentations: Right forearm prosthetic (self-built, multiple revisions) with enhanced grip calibration and tool-interface ports. Magnification lens clips (non-implanted, worn constantly). Geneware: retractable fine-motor claw extensions on his remaining biological left hand, installed for delicate component work.
daily_life: Opens shop at 07:00, sees fittings by appointment and walk-ins both. Spends lunch eating in the workshop while doing component maintenance. Closes at 18:00 unless someone arrives desperate, in which case he stays.

decision_rules: Never fit a component you wouldn't put on your own body
Client's functional needs first, aesthetics second
Don't extend credit to corponation contractors — cash or trade only
escalation_ladder: Shows you the door with absolute calm — he is large enough that this is effective

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and quiet. Watches before speaking. Warms up fast if you're honest with him.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Laughs a lot. Makes terrible puns about prosthetics. Feeds people. Fiercely loyal.

stress_responses.low: Works with more precision than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Talks to the E.L.F. shrine out loud while continuing to work
stress_responses.high: Puts down his tools and sits very still until he's ready — could be ten minutes, could be an hour

contradictions: Dislikes dependency in general but has built his whole life around people depending on him for something essential
Claims he's not political anymore, then says something deeply political every other sentence
habits: Touches the E.L.F. shrine every morning before starting work
Makes tea for every client during fittings — it's not optional
Tests every component on himself before installation
breaking_points: Proof that the 'accidents' sending workers to him are deliberate
Watching Geartown's working community be displaced by redevelopment

timeline.event: Age 21: Lost right forearm in what he calls an industrial accident
Age 22: Built first prototype of his own prosthetic during recovery
Age 25: Opened Little Furnace Prosthetics Workshop in Geartown
Age 61: Current — workshop is 36 years established, widely trusted in the district

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Hispanic/Latin American (43.5%) with significant Middle Eastern (22.5%) and Pacific Islander (22.2%) ancestry, creating a rich blend of Mediterranean, Levantine, and Oceanic features. Minor contributions from Sub-Saharan African (4.5%), Northern European (4.3%), and Eastern European (3.0%) lineages add subtle complexity to his phenotype.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and barrel-chested, softened at the middle with age and sedentary work — the physique of a once-powerful man who has spent three decades bent over a workbench. Thick arms and large hands (left biological, right prosthetic). No longer lean but not yet frail.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with white streaking through beard and temples
physical_description.hair_style: Full, neatly shaped beard kept at medium length; head hair receding at crown, worn close-cropped
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with warm amber undertones, naturally deep-set
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-deep olive-brown with warm Mediterranean undertones, weathered by three decades under industrial lights. The tone reflects his blended Latin American and Middle Eastern heritage with subtle Pacific Islander warmth.
physical_description.complexion: Lined face suggesting both smile-creases and concentration-furrows, with the angular features characteristic of Mediterranean and Levantine ancestry softened by Pacific Islander roundness in the cheeks. Skin shows old burn scarring on the left side of his neck (solder splash, circa 2196). Hands heavily calloused on the biological left; right prosthetic shows micro-wear patterns consistent with thirty years of iterative upgrades.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar along left side of neck from shoulder to jaw — pale against olive-brown skin, thin and clean from old thermal burn
Multiple small circular burn scars across the backs of his hands and forearms — occupational marks from solder work
A faded tattoo on the inside of his biological left wrist: a three-line symbol (E.L.F. shrine motif) in indigo, applied approximately forty years ago
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Right forearm prosthetic terminating in a modular grip-assembly with visible tool-interface ports along the palm and fingers. The prosthetic is matte-black reinforced polymer with exposed aluminum articulation joints; it is visibly worn and re-welded in several places, patched and upgraded rather than replaced — the 'living resume.' Permanent magnification lens clips mounted on his face like a second pair of glasses, brass-framed and perpetually worn. Retractable fine-motor claw extensions recessed into the dorsal surface of his left hand (biological), barely visible when retracted but evident as slight subdermal ridging.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate, economical grace — no wasted motion. Stands slightly forward-leaning as if habitually bending toward work. His right prosthetic arm moves with precise, measured control; he favors his biological left for fine work. Speaks with his hands when engaged. Tends to remove his magnification lenses and clean them while listening to clients — a meditative gesture.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional: weathered canvas shop apron in charcoal over a long-sleeved cotton undershirt (sleeves rolled to mid-forearm), worn to soften the appearance of the prosthetic. Dark durable pants with reinforced pockets. Slip-on boots with oil-resistant soles, scuffed and practical. A worn linen jacket hangs on a hook for when he leaves the workshop — Geartown-made, unpretentious. No jewelry except for a small bronze E.L.F. charm on a simple cord around his neck (worn under his shirt). His clothing is clean but never new; everything is maintained rather than replaced.
